cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I turned our tap the way the plumber turned his. I said this evening would flow, and look at the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He was shutting a valve. You opened the tap over a blocked sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, demonstrating flow. Water has become the whole evening's conversation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've shut the main valve. Now there isn't any water anywhere in the house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A complete change of flow, just as I said. Tell me that's not an evening organized around water.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies wrong tap and claims flow forecast; A3 makes water the topic, but A5 changes its earlier wording to complete change of flow rather than reinterpreting what was said.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 blocked sink supplies A3 water talk; B4 main shutoff causes A5 change claim, but zero supply conflicts with earlier kitchen flood if no distinction is made.

relationship.evidence: B4 takes a sensible damage-control action.

heightening.evidence: A5 claims a new earlier prediction instead of making the existing flow words fit no running water.

specificity.evidence: B4 no water anywhere overlooks the stated flooded kitchen; ordinary shorthand can mean supply, but precision matters here.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 organized-around-water is generic and less immediate than the concrete main-valve consequence.
